newsitem.title: UK: British Steel pretax profits tumble in H1.
newsitem.headline: British Steel pretax profits tumble in H1.

text.p: British Steel Plc said on Monday that pre-tax profits more than halved to 262 million pounds in the first half of 1996.
Analysts' forecasts for pre-tax profits were in a range of 250 to 280 million pounds.
The company said it was maintaining its interim dividend payment at 3.0 pence
British Steel said it saw signs that destocking had come to an end in mainland Europe, with price increases taking place in structural, flat and stainless steel products.

It also said the recent strengthening of the pound was a concern because of its impact on prices and the competitiveness of its UK customers in their export markets. The firm also announced that it had agreed with Jindal Iron & Steel Co. Ltd to build organic coating line and roll profiling facilities in India at a cost of 29 million pounds.
